Dear Nitin,

You asked why I wasn't at the football camp in Goa. I told everyone it was "family stuff". The truth is simpler and worse.

Papa's bakery lost its delivery boy in May, and Mummy said, "It would help if you stayed." Not an order. Just tired. I didn't want a fight, so I said, "Okay, I'll skip the camp." I never told them the coach had picked me specially, or that scouts from the state team were coming.

So I've been delivering bread on the scooter for three weeks. Every morning I pass the ground where the others trained before leaving. And every morning I feel a little angrier, at nobody in particular. Yesterday I snapped at Papa over nothing. He looked confused.

They think I didn't mind. They don't know what I gave up. I'm starting to think that's my fault.

Joseph

That evening he sat with his parents on the terrace. His mother, Sangeeta, asked the questions he hadn't. "Till ten at night? Who else works there? Is it on the main road or in the back lane?"

His father added, "And the rules? You're a minor."

In Marseille, Fatima found a notice in the bakery window: "Weekend help wanted, early mornings." She was fifteen. The bakery was a ten-minute walk from home.

At dinner she told her parents. Her father, Sami, didn't say no. He said, "Let's look at the rules together first."

After dinner they sat at the laptop and read the official government page about work for under-sixteens. There were limits: only light work, only during school holidays, a maximum number of hours, and a parent's written consent.

"Early mornings," her mother said. "How early?"

Fatima called the baker the next day. Five a.m. for the kneading shift. That was not allowed at her age.

"But I can do Saturday afternoons at the counter, in the holidays," Fatima reported. "From two to six."

Sami signed the consent form. "Daylight, near home, and legal. Good."

qa.a: Saturday afternoons in the holidays, from two to six.

qa.a: She may have felt a little disappointed, but also satisfied to find a safe, legal option instead.

qa.q: What else should Fatima and her parents keep an eye on?
qa.a: They should make sure the counter job stays light and within the hours agreed, and speak up if the baker asks for more.

qa.a: Sami seems satisfied and reassured, signing the form because the work is in daylight, near home and legal.
